To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) actinomycin and the other inhibitors suppress the synthesis of RNA, but not protein or sterols, in the presence of oxygen, but not in its absence; (2) actinomycines and the other inhibitors do not affect amino acid activation in vitro, nor amino acid incorporation into protein in the presence of the inhibitors; and (3) the inhibitory effects are reversed by the addition of glucose to the medium in which the inhibitors are present.
the biosynthetic processes of protein and sterol synthesis are inhibited by actinomycin in Sarcoma 37 tumor cells only under oxidative conditions.
actinomycin and the other inhibitors we used inhibited synthesis of total protein in the absence, but not the presence of glucose.

the effect of actinomy-cins and other inhibitors of RNA biosynthesis on synthesis of protein, sterols and RNA.
the effect of actinomicin D on the biosynthesis of protein and sterol by Sarcoma 37 ascitie-tumor cells in vitro.
the role of RNA synthesis in the biosynthetic activities of Sarcoma 37 ascitic-tumor cells, which are maintained in vitro in the presence of 20% serum and 5% glucose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition of sterol synthesis by actinomycin is a consequence of the inhibition of RNA synthesis.
the actinomycin effect is a consequence of its inhibition of RNA synthesis.
RNA synthesis is required for the synthesis of sterols and protein in Sarcoma 37 ascitic tumor cells under conditions of oxygenation.

the biosynthesis of protein and sterol is inhibited by actinomycin in the absence of a source of energy other than the oxidation of glucose.

the inhibition of RNA synthesis is not a direct result of the inhibition of RNA.
